english.title: Make damaging disclosure of protected information / document / article
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having come into possession of

(A)_[information,]_
(B)_[a document,]_
(C)_[an article,]_

in circumstances as mentioned in section 5(1) of the Official Secrets Act 1989, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CIRCUMSTANCES..), disclosed it without lawful authority knowing, or having reasonable cause to believe, that it was protected against disclosure by sections 1 to 4 of that Act, that it had come into your possession in those circumstances and, that disclosure being damaging, you made it knowing, or having reasonable cause to believe, that it would be damaging
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 5(2) and 10(1) of the Official Secrets Act 1989.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
having come into possession of information / document / article
in circumstances as mentioned in section 5(1) of the Act
disclosed it without lawful authority
knowing / having reasonable cause to believe that it was protected against disclosure by sections 1 to 4 of that Act

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence cannot be used if the disclosure would be an offence under sections 1 to 4 of the Official Secrets Act 1989.

other.penalty:
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
